text: The contractor shall submit an innovative cylinder tracking plan with their proposal at no additional cost to the Government. The plan must include, but is not limited to: method for data entry and extraction, mechanism for data entry, how and when the Government will be able to extract data, type of data entered and stored, limits on access to Government employees, technology/software requiring connection to the Government network, perpetual delivery, pick-up and location data per cylinder, and any other reports related to cylinder tracking that may be beneficial for the ordering activity. If the the contractor has an impending tracking system that is not yet fully operational, they must include a timeline for implementation that coincides with the phase-in timeline, provided the system will be fully operational by the conclusion of the contract transition.

citations.quote:
The contractor shall submit an innovative plan with their proposal for tracking medical 
 gas cylinders being delivered to and from the ordering activity.

The cylinder tracking 
 plan shall be provided by the contractor with no additional cost to the Government.
The cylinder tracking plan shall include, but is not limited to:

a) Method used for data entry and extraction (i.e. web-based portal, Microsoft Excel 
spreadsheet, SharePoint, email, etc.);

b) Mechanism for data entry (i.e. barcode scanning, handwriting serial numbers, 
photos, etc.);
c) How and when Government will be able to extract data;
d) What type of data will be entered and stored;
e) Limits on access to Government employees, if applicable;

f) Any technology, equipment, software, etc. that requires connection to the 
Government network, if applicable;
Any other pertinent information related to the cylinder tracking plan

text: The contractor shall submit a Project Management Plan (PMP) with their proposal that demonstrates an understanding of the scope, schedule, and service level requirements. The PMP must include: a communications and task matrix (POCs and roles/responsibilities), individuals responsible for deliverables and their timely delivery, a preliminary delivery, install, and user acceptance schedule with task interdependencies, estimates of time for critical tasks, processes for tracking and communicating delivery progress, installation, and equipment acceptance, and a description of approach to identify and resolve potential project problems.

citations.quote:
14.1.  The contractor shall submit a Project Management Plan (PMP) with their proposal that 
 clearly demonstrates an understanding of the scope, schedule and service level 
 requirements of this contract.  At a minimum, the PMP shall include the following items: 
a) Communications and task matrix providing point-of-contact information and 
identifying and delineating the roles and responsibilities of key contractor personnel 
and resources; 
b) Individual responsible for providing the required contract deliverables and how 
the contractor will ensure the deliverables are delivered on time;

Estimate of how much time each critical task is expected to take and when each 
is scheduled to begin and end (time period in workdays or weeks);

Outline of processes used to track and communicate delivery progress, 
installation, and document equipment acceptance;

Description of approach to identify the warning signs of potential project 
problems and their resolution process.
